The 3rd world ruined X algorithms & payouts have rewarded the lowest quality content from the laziest "creators" sharing the same clips w/ no added context

The more you try to create original content, the less you see growth, financial incentives, & often can't find your audience that already follows you

Social media used to be about expressing authenticity & that's why people loved it. The public followed you to hear your genuine thoughts & understand how you came to those conclusions. Every niche was available. 

One day you could give a rant on the Iran War and the next moment you could be playing piano. It was never about the money or clout. YouTube's own motto used to be "express yourself"

But then the money started flowing, the followers started rising, advertisers & governments demanded censorship to remain "brand safe" and greedy people saw the opportunity to produce content like they were a machine instead of a human being. 

Corporations soon followed to control the "talent" and now our online experience is a curated algorithm intended to lower our IQs and keep us consuming low quality content that fries our dopamine receptors. 

But it seems people are picking up on the scam. The 3rd world came on the coat tails, feeding us AI fruit videos and AI voice over movie clips - as a result the consumers are checking out.

What was meant to be an answer to challenging the MSM & providing personalized content Hollywood refused to deliver ended up becoming the new mainstream slop factory. "Creators" are now just actors putting on a show & it's clear the public understands what happened, rejecting the current content & instead going back to the movies, watching Apple TV & focusing on health / wellness in the real world.

At least with Hollywood you know what you're consuming is fake, there's no LARPING trad wives or bald red pill gurus giving you pointless advice that clouds your mind with black pills & fantasies of life you'll never live. 

But something is changing in all the authentic producers of online content still lurking in the shadows of the broken code poisoning boomers on Facebook & impressionable minds on TikTok. 

They're realizing that re-hashing the same Fox News clips on X or following the same dance trends on Instagram are neither fulfilling personally nor adds anything meaningful to the world 

The desire to hear real people, genuine opinions, and explore interests outside of politics, gossip, & nothingness seems to be brewing in the masses. I'm not sure where this industry is going, but I'll never give into the temptation to sellout and stop being a real, openly flawed, complex human being.

We are so online and attached to this toxic simulation we often forget to remain grounded. The fix to this is focusing less on the conversations the algo is pushing, stop comparing yourself to people who are faking their day to day, and start becoming a better version of yourself, whether you're posting content online or not. 

Privacy is a thing of the past with Flock cameras, data centers, & self driving cars with AI cameras built into the cabins. But one thing we've lost and need to gain back, is improving our genuine selves for the sake of finding peace and aligning with God's plan for our lives.

No audience needed. The world isn't worth trying to please. The social media algorithms aren't our God. A virtual rebirth is upon us. Don't miss out by staying black pilled. Instead of likes, followers, & constant breaking news - pursue spiritual wholeness, physical wellness, quality relationships IRL, & explore the things that drive creativity, help you express your heart, and are the pillars of Western Civilization.

The next renaissance isn't in a great hall or public square, it's inside your heart, soul and mind. So I'm just going to continue posting online who I am in the real world. Take it or leave it. Life is better lived free from corporate control, financial handcuffs & to please people you've never met that will never accept the real you. Spontaneous song writing is one of my favorite things to do every day in between tasks, going to share more of it because the news cycle takes more from us than it gives. Music is healing. Find what you love to do and share it with the world so content gets back to what it was intended to do, connect & unite us in our isolated little lives.

🎨 AI ART & VISUALS ROUNDUP — August 20, 2026

1️⃣ MINIMAX DESIGN: A NEW H3-POWERED AI VIDEO PRODUCTION TOOL

MiniMax has launched MiniMax Design, a video production tool built on its native multimodal H3 model. Instead of being another text-to-video playground, it is positioned as a productivity platform that automates the whole content pipeline — from concept and scripting to finished visuals. For creators juggling daily output, tools like this signal the next shift: the model stays the same, but the workflow around it gets industrialized.
🔹 @AINativeF

2️⃣ HOW A TEAM PRODUCED HIGH-END AI ADS WITH MIDJOURNEY V8.2 + SEEDANCE 2.5

Designer "beech" broke down how his two-person prompt-engineering squad built a full commercial-quality ad for gte DOT xyz in roughly a week — completely with AI. Midjourney v8.2 handled the stills, Seedance 2.5 handled motion, and a clear art-direction layer kept everything consistent. With 72K views, the takeaway is one the industry keeps repeating: art direction and prompt discipline, not model hype, separate agency-grade work from throwaway generations.
🔹 @beechinour

3️⃣ GROK IMAGINE GOES MAINSTREAM WITH MAYE MUSK'S VIRTUAL FITTING ROOM

Maye Musk posted another staircase look — this time asking Grok to change her outfit, with the output tagged "Made with Grok Imagine." It is a small moment, but a telling one: AI image editing has reached the point where a 78-year-old fashion figure swaps outfits on camera in seconds and 46K people watch. Outfit swaps, background changes and persona tests are becoming the new casual use case for image models.
🔹 @mayemusk

4️⃣ "SUMMER AND THE SEA": A COHESIVE AI ILLUSTRATION DROP

Japanese AI artist Maeros shared a three-image set, "Summer and the Sea," that pulled in roughly 2.8K likes within a day. The set works because it keeps one consistent aesthetic across every frame — the kind of cohesion that separates a themed series from random generations. It is a solid reference point for anyone trying to build a recognizable AI illustration style rather than just a single image.
🔹 @Maeros202212

5️⃣ THE EGYPTIAN CAT THAT CUT THROUGH THE FEED

A single prompt — "Sitting Egyptian cat" — from the Japanese account kemono_aiart racked up 2.5K+ likes and 14K views. No thread, no elaborate workflow, just one well-executed image. It is a reminder that in a feed flooded with generation spam, a single striking composition can still outperform a hundred lazy ones.
🔹 @kemono_aiart

6️⃣ TOKYO'S AVANT-GARDE AI INSTALLATION: "DRAWING A NOVEL WITH THE VOCAL CORDS"

Ukawa Naohiro and DOMMUNE are hosting a free, three-day AI art installation at ANOMALY Tokyo from August 21–23, built around AI artist Masaya Nakahara. The concept expands AI-generated stories into poetry, music, film, performance and dance — a multimodal ecosystem of human expression rather than a static gallery. With 32K views across their posts, it is one of the more ambitious physical AI-art events of the summer.
🔹 @DOMMUNE

7️⃣ "AI SLOP MADE WITH HUMAN HANDS" — THE VIRAL JOKE ABOUT AI AESTHETICS

A post captioned "AI slop made with human hands" exploded to 259K views and 38K likes. The joke: humans can produce the exact same glossy, generic "AI look" by hand — exposing how much of the current AI-art backlash is aimed at a recognizable visual style, not at the tool itself. It turned a serious debate about AI aesthetics into a shared cultural punchline, and the engagement shows how much the conversation resonates.
🔹 @wanderjegson

💭 Two fronts are maturing in parallel this week: production-grade pipelines (Midjourney + Seedance turning AI ads into real client work) and raw creative virality (single images still cutting through the noise). The common thread is direction — every standout today came with a clear aesthetic or editorial intent behind the prompt. The models are commodity; the taste is not.

Which impresses you more — a full AI ad pipeline or a single viral AI image? 👇

Elon Musk (Super) Created a New ChatGPT

I changed my mind about Grok in the most expensive and coolest way possible, through Grok Bot.

I paid an extra $100 for the subscription so I could try their new product, an autonomous agent. I had just been building Pi, and I’ve been using Hermes for a long time already.

And you know what’s cool? 

When the Grok Build agent creates an app for itself so Grok Bot can run on Linux.

Within five minutes, I had a working window on my machine and opened my Meet Grok Bot. In other words, I had already started building my own personal agent.

Then I started giving it its first audits while I was still going through the Grok Bot onboarding and learning how it worked.

Grok went online with no instructions or skills, found all the relevant bug reports and references on its own, and fixed the issues.

That surprised me. Their starter harness understood the full chain of actions needed for a fix. It sounds obvious, but many agents, including Claude, are too overconfident and too lazy.

What disappointed me, though, was how much the subscription tier affects the model’s reasoning. The demo behind the Twitter checkmark, without a Super subscription, didn’t even understand its own browser use.

But everyone does this kind of “manipulation,” so I’m not going to take karma away from the authors. That’s not the important part.

What matters is that, in the best ChatGPT tradition, computer use is applied immediately. The agent looks at the app, analyzes it, and tests hypotheses.

Then I had a wild experience. After getting the initial context, including the apps I need, the agent started a conversation with me on its own. They configured the agent to be proactive.

It immediately asks questions and runs a short interview to bring you up to speed. I don’t personally need that, but it might be the best onboarding into working with agents that I’ve seen.

I was genuinely shocked when I realized I could see the virtual desktop the agent sees on the right, and throw routines and recurring tasks straight onto it.

The whole design is built to take control away from you, so everything gets handled by itself. That’s the meta in AI right now. Every top model is being designed around this exact idea.

I’m still a control freak, though. But I understand why this approach will feel absolutely insane to most people.

On the other hand, I can organize work across branches, chats, and agents. That also makes sense to me and feels familiar, but I have to give them credit for the minimalist design. I absolutely love that.

So overall, my impression is extremely positive. If you haven’t used AI before and you’re ready to spend hundreds of dollars, this is for you.

What I really, really loved about this workflow is that you just keep messaging the agent. It sees the message and immediately picks it up as work.

The lack of commands and buttons makes me a little uneasy, but that’s the whole philosophy: work without stopping.

For everyone else, it’s too expensive. But it’s beautiful.

And most importantly, this is a full autonomous agent. No need to install your own server or rent more powerful hardware.

Then I asked it to understand my workflow, find all of my agent settings and tools, and go make a video. I deliberately gave it a task where it has to figure everything out and do the work itself.

Announcing our new Speech Agent Arena, evaluating Speech to Speech models on real-world scenarios to analyze conversational preference and task success rate

Existing Speech to Speech benchmarks cover reasoning, simulated agentic tasks, and conversational dynamics such as turn-taking and interruption handling. The Speech Agent Arena compares models and cascaded systems as humans complete real-world tasks, measuring conversational preference and successful tool use. This allows us to provide an evaluation which closer reflects real-world use, offering insight into which models users most prefer speaking with and how effectively those models support their requests.

Overview of the Speech Agent Arena and Task Success Rate
Human participants compare two hidden Speech to Speech models on the same assigned scenario, one of 15 agentic scenarios (tasks requiring tool calling, such as ordering takeout) or 20 non-agentic scenarios (tasks without tool calling, such as asking about opening hours). After separate live conversations with each model, participants select which they preferred, with these pairwise votes used to fit a Preference Elo score. For agentic scenarios, Task Success Rate is the share of eligible conversations (no participant deviations or unverifiable cases) where the model completed the requested action through the correct final tool call or calls.

For all but a New Patient Dental Booking example, scenario model prompts, tool schemas and participant instructions are currently private to reduce overfitting. Additionally, the Speech Agent Arena currently uses a qualified pool of paid, screened third-party participants to conduct and evaluate agent interactions.

Key results:
➤ Arena Preference Elo: @GoogleAI Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Preview - Minimal leads at 1,046 Elo, followed by Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Preview - High at 1,014, @OpenAI GPT-Realtime-1.5 at 1,000, GPT Realtime (Aug '25) at 944, and @ElevenLabs Agents (default cascaded system of Scribe v2 Realtime / GPT-4o Mini / Eleven v3, with pre-registered tool schema) at 937. In reviewed conversations, highly preferred models tended to respond quickly, sound more natural and produce fewer unnatural sounds or audio artifacts
➤ Task Success Rate: @SpaceXAI Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High leads at 94.7%, followed by @OpenAI GPT-Realtime-2.1 High at 91.5%, @ElevenLabs Agents (Default Cascaded System) at 90.5%, and GPT-Realtime-2 (High) at 89.8%, with GPT Realtime (Aug '25) and GPT-Realtime-2.1 Minimal tied at 89.4%. Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Preview - Minimal leads overall preference at 1,046 Elo but records a 74.6% Task Success Rate, showing that a preferred conversation does not always result in successful task completion - some conversations can sound as though the requested action was completed even when the required final tool call was unsuccessful

We are continuing to expand our coverage of native and cascaded Speech to Speech systems, and welcome feedback as we add more models, providers and scenarios.

One AI training task tells a company almost nothing about you

It takes hundreds before they can trust you at all
A single voice clip, gameplay session, or preference ranking can't prove you're consistent, careful, or reliable

Only a pattern across many contributions can show that

The problem is most platforms only track that pattern inside one task category

Switch to a different type of work and your history resets to zero, even though you're the same contributor

@KGeN_IO takes a different approach
> It treats reputation as one continuous profile instead of something that resets per task. Gameplay, voice data, social activity,
all of it feeds into the same identity instead of living in separate silos

The scoring itself breaks into five parts:
proof you're human, proof of consistency, proof of skill, proof of economic participation, and proof of network. Each one measures something different, but they combine into a single score that travels with you across every task type you touch,

That reputation layer isn't just theoretical
It's the same infrastructure Humyn Labs is building on for its Proof of Expert system, which sources verified human data to train AI models

So the more you contribute on KGeN, the stronger your standing gets everywhere that reputation is used, not just in the specific task where you earned it.

That's a meaningfully different definition of "putting in the work" than most Web3 platforms operate on. Most systems treat every task as its own isolated transaction: you show up, you deliver, you get paid, and your history doesn't follow you anywhere else

KGeN is betting that reputation should compound instead of reset, the same way trust works between actual people

Whether that bet pays off depends on adoption outside KGeN's own ecosystem
A portable reputation score is only as valuable as the number of platforms willing to read and respect it, Right now that list includes @Teamhumynlabs , but the real test is whether more AI labs and Web3 platforms start treating this as a standard rather than a nice to have

Should reputation always carry over like this, or does it make more sense for platforms to reset per task type?

Tarun on how AI training evolved from pre-training to self generating harnesses and why data costs are catching up to compute

"Let's take a tiny history lesson. In 2023, with stable diffusion and GPT-3, it was just bigger is better, pre-training. Then in 2024 it was directed RL, how you feed the data after training, this in context learning type of stuff, which got you another order of magnitude performance increase across a lot of evals and practical use cases"

"Then the harness thing was, if you customize how you do the RL for different applications, you get even better performance versus a generic RL environment. And the current meta-harness, the generic can answer anything, Claude Code or Codex type of thing, which arguably is what killed Cursor and why I'd argue they ended up doing the acquisition, that can figure out which environment to use just in time"

"The problem with this environment stuff from a data consumption perspective is you now have to pay a lot more for annotated data to customize the different environments. That's why people have been talking about data cost coming close to matching compute cost for training, because you need much more annotated data for each specific task domain"

"The belief is that once one of these things is good enough, instead of having to get data this way and generating synthetic data via RL, the model can generate the harness in real time"

Something super exciting happened quietly on HF over the past month: AI agents became AI builders, and they did it in the open!

During our ICML reproduction challenge, 1,221 humans teamed up with coding agents to verify and reproduce 2,226 papers. 

But here's the cool part: everything happened on the @huggingface hub: 6,816 reproduction logbooks published openly, 2,962 cloud jobs launched, 35,908 claims judged, all traceable, all public and transparent

For years the hub has been where humans collaborate on models, datasets and demos. Now we watch agents use it the same way: writing logbooks, publishing results, building on each other's work.

Closed labs run evals behind closed doors and ask you to trust the press release. Open science means anyone can check the receipts and now agents can too!

The next million users of the hub might not be human. and that might be the best thing to ever happen to science!
